unit: lines of Rust in kernel/src, without blank lines and comments, both architectures (scripts/kernel_budget.py)

raised.why: the first budget (850-KRN-0145): the measured size and about 10% of room; a raise is a commit of its own that names the mechanism and why it cannot live in user space (MC-1.2)

000-KRN-0104: the derivation tree's index and revocation in steps (kernel/src/scheduler/tree.rs, about 200 lines): which capability derives from which is the kernel's own state (MC-3.3), so the walk that bounds a revocation (MC-5.4) cannot live in user space

100000-KRN-0171 (about 70 lines in kernel/src; the table itself is common/nodes.rs, outside it): the platform nodes' table, built from the device tree or the firmware's tables, and the checks of PLATFORM_MMIO and PLATFORM_NODE_IRQ. Which registers and lines a task may hold is the kernel's grant (MC-3.1, MC-3.3), and the check that a page holds no other device's registers, no RAM and none the kernel drives needs the kernel's view of all of them, so it cannot live in user space. 000-KRN-0220 (10 lines): each CPU turning its caches on and its CR0 recorded are processor state only the kernel sets. 7320 lines after both; about 80 of room.

100004-PRT-0014 (about 87 lines in kernel/src/arch/aarch64/cpu.rs, most of them assembly): a kernel entered at EL2 leaves it for EL1, the boot CPU and the secondaries alike, since U-Boot with TF-A starts EFI applications at EL2 on the Allwinner boards and the PinePhone, and EDK2 does where the core has EL2. Setting EL2's controls (HCR_EL2, the counter's, stage 2 off, the GICv3 system registers, the ID registers EL1 reads), giving EL1 a map and its MMU before the kernel's own, and the eret to EL1 are the processor's state below the kernel, which only the kernel at entry can set (MC-1.2). 7482 lines after it; about 18 of room.

000-KRN-0231 (33 lines in kernel/src/scheduler.rs: move_waiting, relist, a task's home and the return in select): an application whose wait ended borrows an idle CPU while its own runs a system-band task, and goes back as it waits again. Which CPU a task runs on is the scheduler's decision, taken under its lock at the moment the task becomes ready, so it cannot live in user space; without it a 10 ms sleep ended 30-60 ms late behind the compositor's frame copies in QEMU. 000-KRN-0232 (17 lines): each task's state written each second where QEMU's monitor reads it when a wait runs out, since a stuck system has no task to ask; the lines are written by the harness. 7533 lines after both; about 67 of room.

100004-PRT-0015 (74 lines in kernel/src/arch/aarch64: sunxi_wdt.rs and watchdog.rs, and the feed, start and stops): the Allwinner SoCs' watchdog, armed with the tick and fed every second from the boot CPU's tick, stopped before a halt the kernel chose, a reboot and a power-off, as x86's chipset watchdog is (000-KRN-0076, 213-KRN-0125). Its point is to restart a board whose kernel froze: fed by a task, it would also be fed by a system whose kernel still schedules that task and nothing else, and it must be stopped by the kernel's own halt; and no task may hold its registers, which could stop it. 7640 lines after it; about 60 of room.
